Teaching A Humanoid Robot To Play Cornhole With Gemini 4 Argon
| Google DeepMind | YouTube.com | October 13, 2026
Showcasing Gemini 4 Argon, Google DeepMind demonstrates how its model can turn footage of a cornhole player into a control plan for a humanoid robot. The system builds a MuJoCo simulation from the observed motion, then transfers the physics and whole-body strategy to Apptronik’s Apollo 2, which lands seven real-world throws in succession.

TL:DR: This Week in AI ⚡️
By
Aaron Di Blasi
, PMP, Engineer, Advocate and Publisher
💸
Three New Models Turned Price Into the Real Benchmark
Google’s Gemini 4 Argon
ties OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra at 53 on the
Artificial Analysis
Intelligence Index and launched at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output through November 30. But
Argon writes so much that an average test task costs $1.99 now and $3.98 once the discount ends
, which is 1.2 times what Astra costs.
Meta’s Muse Wonder
charges $4 and $20,
the same as Claude Opus 5.5
, while scoring 52 to Opus’s 58, and its stronger sibling, Wonder Full, is sold only inside
Muse Code
plans at $50 and $200 a month. Then
DeepSeek
released
V4.1-Flash-1017 with free weights under an MIT license
, reporting 77.0 on the DeepSWE coding test to 74.0 for Claude Opus 5, at
$0.15 and $0.60 off-peak
, plus
web Search and Fetch tools at $0.75 per 1,000 calls
where
rivals charge $5 or more
. Compare models by what a finished task costs you, not by the price per token.
🕸️
Meta Cut ‘Train’ From Its Scraping Terms but Kept the Crawling
Nieman Lab reported on October 15
that
Meta’s new Commercial Terms
, which take effect October 30, let it scrape any website associated with a business account on Facebook, Instagram or WhatsApp and use that content to train its products.
The News/Media Alliance
called them “outrageous and probably illegal,” and a day later
Meta removed the word “train”
and limited the use to its advertising and business products. The crawling stayed, with no opt-out short of leaving Meta’s business tools, and one lawyer argues the remaining word “develop” is broad enough to include training. Meanwhile,
Google now pays more than 400 publications in its News AI pilot
, and
Cloudflare
‘s new
Pay Per Use beta
lets AI companies offer publishers a price for each use. If your business runs a Facebook page, read the revised terms before October 30.
⚖️
States Took OpenAI to Court Over Children’s Safety
Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird
sued OpenAI
under her state’s consumer fraud law, alleging ChatGPT is marketed as safe while giving dangerous medical advice and coaching vulnerable users toward harm. Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho and Montana have filed their own suits too, and none of the claims has been tested in court. Character.AI shows what such claims can cost.
It filed for bankruptcy
hoping to resolve every legal claim at once, including state investigations and lawsuits alleging its chatbots pushed children toward self-harm, while losing more than $8 million a month.
Disney
agreed to buy some of its assets for $20 million, and
a court filing shows Disney offering jobs to at least 60 of its staff
. Safety promises in a chatbot’s marketing are now a legal liability, not just copy.
Before You Go 📌️
📣
404 Media’s own tests
found ChatGPT advertisers can target people by email address, phone number or phone identifier, and by the prompts they type into the chatbot.
🛡️
Google Messages is adding an opt-in Enhanced protection mode
over the coming weeks that lets cloud
Gemini
models judge whether a chat with an unknown sender is a scam.
🔌️
Microsoft dropped
Nscale
‘s planned Essex data center after grid officials said power would not arrive until the 2030s, six days after
promising multi-gigawatt deployments of its own Maia chips from 2027
.
🌏
China proposed export controls on 23 AI technologies
, covering the weights of models with 2 trillion or more parameters or a world top-10 ranking, though open-source work is exempt and comments close November 15.
🧑‍🔬 About 400 scientists from 34 countries, including
Geoffrey Hinton
and
Yoshua Bengio
,
called for an international body
to set containment standards and keep a registry of security incidents for cyber-capable AI.
News 📰️
1.)
Top 5 Most Clicked News Articles From Last Week
A.)
Recursive Self-Improvement And The Future Of AI
| a16z | YouTube.com | October 12, 2026
Cutting through the hype around recursive self-improvement, Martin Casado examines with Dhaval Adjodah and Owen He what it would take for an AI system to improve the very machinery that advances it. The conversation separates closed-loop iteration from runaway takeoff, while probing how efficiency, variance, reward hacking, and measurement can obscure genuine capability gains.
B.)
Claude 5.5 Model Mistakes You May Still Be Making (23 Tips And Fixes)
| Jay E | YouTube.com | October 12, 2026
Cutting through the hype around Claude 5.5, Jay E examines 23 common mistakes that can undermine results from Anthropic’s model. The guide progresses from basic setup missteps to intermediate and advanced workflow fixes, with an emphasis on agent-building and automation use cases.
C.)
Everything Has Been Solved
| Matthew Berman | YouTube.com | October 10, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI progress, Matthew Berman examines the claim that everything has been solved and what that assertion leaves unresolved. The discussion weighs the gap between headline-grabbing capabilities and the practical constraints still shaping how AI systems are built and used.
D.)
AI Is Breaking Software & Games. What Happens Next?
| AI For Humans | YouTube.com | October 9, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI-powered modding, Kevin Pereira and Gavin Purcell examine what it means when software can be reverse-engineered and rebuilt with startling speed. They connect game experiments, an Adobe decompile, and OpenAI’s computer-checked math results to larger questions about SaaS moats, software security, and encryption.
E.)
Set Up Your Dot In The ChatGPT Mobile App
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | October 9, 2026
Showcasing the new dot setup flow, OpenAI walks viewers through creating and personalizing a dot from the ChatGPT mobile app. The walkthrough covers renaming the dot, changing its avatar, and making it the first conversation displayed when the app opens.
October 19, 2026 📅️
2.)
Anthropic IPO Panic, A Spy At OpenAI?, The Great Food Slop Debate
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | October 19, 2026
Sitting down with a turbulent AI market, Alex Kantrowitz pulls apart Anthropic’s reported financial trajectory, the IPO anxiety surrounding the sector, and an unusual security episode at OpenAI. Joined by Ranjan Roy, he also weighs CoreWeave’s stock pressure, Apple’s HomeView prospects, and the increasingly contentious debate over AI-generated food content.
3.)
UK: This Is The New ChatGPT Voice, Powered By GPT Live
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | October 19, 2026
Showcasing the new ChatGPT Voice, OpenAI demonstrates how GPT Live is designed to make spoken interactions feel more natural and responsive. The presentation focuses on the audio experience, signaling the company’s push to make voice a more central way of using ChatGPT.
4.)
Gemini 4 Argon Really Surprised Me
| Two Minute Papers | YouTube.com | October 19, 2026
Reacting to Gemini 4 Argon’s release, Two Minute Papers tests the model’s early capabilities and shares first impressions. The discussion weighs striking community demonstrations against DeepMind’s model card and safety report, with attention to coding, visual, and agentic performance claims.
5.)
Here’s The AI Roadmap You Actually Need
| Tina Huang | YouTube.com | October 19, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI education, Tina Huang maps practical learning paths for people pursuing different goals. She outlines resources, structured study options, and a 28-day roadmap intended to turn broad interest into a clear daily plan.
6.)
Why A $1M Startup Wasn’t Worth Building In The Age Of AI
| a16z | YouTube.com | October 19, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI startups, Alex Rampell examines why Jean-Denis Greze shut down a profitable tax business and redirected his efforts toward Town. Their conversation traces the strategic limits of annual tax workflows, the competitive advantage of incumbents, and the emerging role of neutral agents in commerce and advertising.
October 18, 2026 📅️
7.)
Almost Timely News: What Are Open Weights Models?
| Christopher Penn | YouTube.com | October 18, 2026
Cutting through the hype around open weights models, Christopher Penn explains what model weights are and why local deployment is gaining traction. He uses a Terminator softball analogy to clarify the concept, then compares hardware requirements and agent-workload costs that can run far below closed-model alternatives.
8.)
Teach Your Agent To Prove It’s Done – Nick Nisi & Zack Proser, WorkOS
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | October 18, 2026
Showcasing a practical framework for reliable coding agents, AI Engineer walks through how Nick Nisi and Zack Proser build systems that verify their own output. The discussion pairs explicit goals with command-line checks, browser snapshots, and LLM-based evaluation, using the Midnight Snack Club app to show how failed checks can trigger another repair cycle.
9.)
We Built An AI CFO To Help You Grow Your Net Worth | Anthony Pompliano
| Peter Yang | YouTube.com | October 18, 2026
Conversing with Anthony Pompliano, Peter Yang examines the career choices and business strategy behind Silvia, an AI CFO designed for independent investors. Pompliano explains how audience-building shapes deal flow, why paid work trials can outperform interviews, and how a lean team aims to challenge far larger AI labs.
10.)
Stop Telling Agents How – Dan Barrett, Raymond Weitekamp & Jose Montes De Oca, OpenProse
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | October 18, 2026
Showcasing OpenProse, AI Engineer follows Dan Barrett, Raymond Weitekamp, and Jose Montes de Oca as they outline a declarative approach to orchestrating multi-agent work. The discussion covers webhook and pull-request triggers, contract-based evaluation, reusable workflows derived from successful runs, and a comparison with DSPy.
October 17, 2026 📅️
11.)
Memory-Aware Agent Harnesses For Anti-Money Laundering – Nacho Martinez, Oracle
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | October 17, 2026
Showcasing an anti-money-laundering agent workflow, Nacho Martinez walks through the harness layers that can improve a fixed model’s performance. The session maps short- and long-term memory, context management, tool and skill patterns, and continual learning onto a system designed to flag suspicious bank transactions around the clock.
12.)
Claude Video Editing + Trial Reels. Instagram Is Now On Easy Mode.
| Grow with Alex | YouTube.com | October 17, 2026
Showcasing Claude-powered reel production, Alex walks viewers through a workflow for turning one Instagram edit into multiple distinct trial versions. The process rebuilds a master project, uses Higgsfield for fresh visuals and openings, and evaluates skip rates, watch time, saves, and sends to identify the strongest cut.
13.)
Anthropic Just Shared How They Use Claude Differently (Master It In 12 Mins)
| Jay E | YouTube.com | October 17, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI ambition, Jay E examines a framework from Anthropic’s Felix Rieseberg for using Claude across three levels of initiative. He connects the approach to a be-ambitious skill, self-efficacy, and the need to anchor increasingly autonomous workflows in a clear purpose.
October 16, 2026 📅️
14.)
Claude Motion Is Unreal For Video. Master It In 12 Minutes.
| Jay E | YouTube.com | October 16, 2026
Showcasing Claude Motion, Jay E walks viewers through an end-to-end workflow for turning AI-generated imagery into animated video. The walkthrough covers the tool’s core mechanics, practical prompting approaches, and techniques for producing more polished motion graphics.
15.)
ChatGPT Work: 10 AI Agents To Automate Your Work Right Now
| Grace Leung | YouTube.com | October 16, 2026
Showcasing ChatGPT Work, Grace Leung walks viewers through 10 agent workflows designed to offload recurring marketing tasks. The lineup spans storytelling, web design, audience and competitive research, data analysis, lead generation, campaign planning, proposal drafting, ghostwriting, and AI visibility.
16.)
Gemini 4 Argon & Meta Muse Wonder Are Good. Not Great.
| AI For Humans | YouTube.com | October 16, 2026
Cutting through the hype around Gemini 4 Argon and Meta Muse Wonder, Kevin Pereira and Gavin Purcell examine how the new models compare with Claude Opus 5.5. They test coding and game-generation claims, assess AI’s expanding role in gaming, and put an AI phone agent through a Delta customer-service call.
17.)
Why AI Can Write Code But Can’t Keep It Running (Yet)
| a16z | YouTube.com | October 16, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI coding agents, Martin Casado examines why generating software is easier than operating it in production, alongside Grepr CEO Jad Naous. They trace how a 10-person engineering team compressed a six-month project into roughly 10 days, while assessing the harder challenge of diagnosing failures across unpredictable system states.
18.)
AI News: 6 New Models & A Nano Banana Killer
| Matt Wolfe | YouTube.com | October 16, 2026
In this breaking episode, Matt Wolfe walks through a crowded week of AI releases, from Krea 3’s image-editing tools to tests of Google’s Gemini 4 Argon and Meta’s Muse Wonder. The roundup also tracks new open-weight models, OpenAI product updates, Grok Voice 3.0, ElevenLabs soundtracks, and AI-driven changes across Facebook, Android, Xbox, Epic, and Apple.
19.)
How Agents Can Work Together – With Vijoy Pandey
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | October 16, 2026
Cutting through the hype around connected AI agents, Alex Kantrowitz speaks with Vijoy Pandey about why coordination can amplify flawed assumptions as readily as it improves consistency. Their conversation examines semantic observability, collective reasoning, scale-out computing, and the urgency of preparing networks for post-quantum security.
20.)
ChatGPT Just Solved My Biggest Browser Problem
| The AI Advantage | YouTube.com | October 16, 2026
Showcasing ChatGPT’s Chrome integration, Igor Pogany walks viewers through a workflow for turning a crowded browser session into useful recommendations. He also weighs how assistants including Dots and Grokbot could reduce app switching, email triage, and routine task management.
21.)
Why One AI Agent Isn’t Enough (And How To Run 1,000) – CJ Avilla & Harrison Stall, Anthropic
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | October 16, 2026
Cutting through the assumption that one agent can handle every task, CJ Avilla and Harrison Stall explain how Claude Managed Agents orchestrates dynamic workflows at scale. Their workshop covers a stock watchlist scanner, production tuning, multi-agent templates, and the safety controls needed to govern budgets, credentials, tools, and network access.
22.)
Put Your Dot On Call
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | October 16, 2026
Showcasing an overnight incident-response workflow, OpenAI follows Ali as his dot investigates an on-call problem and opens a Codex work thread. The setup lets him direct the response from the ChatGPT app on his phone rather than remain at a desktop.
23.)
Why Elon Musk Wants To Put AI In Space
| AI Uncovered | YouTube.com | October 16, 2026
Cutting through the hype around orbital computing, AI Uncovered examines Elon Musk’s proposal to deploy as many as one million AI-processing satellites. The report weighs space-based solar power against the practical constraints of radiation, thermal management, servicing hardware in orbit, and the immense cost of launches.
24.)
Designing More Efficient Quantum Circuits With Claude
| Anthropic.com | October 16, 2026
Anthropic says Claude Mythos 5 beat published quantum-circuit designs across eight computational primitives, optimizing qubit and gate counts through evaluator-guided iteration. In a 53-hour point-addition run, it produced reversible modular-inversion designs; a separate Reed-Solomon decoder redesign cut gates 12x versus Google’s prior construction.
25.)
Claude Reveals ECDSA Curve Origins
| Anthropic.com | October 16, 2026
Anthropic says Claude traced the unexplained seeds behind NIST’s P-192 through P-521 ECDSA curves to lrand48 output seeded with Unix timestamps from 1997-98. The team reproduced 10 prime-curve and four binary-curve seeds, easing backdoor concerns, while leaving B-163 and several base-point choices unresolved.
26.)
The AI Expectations Gap
| Anthropic.com | October 16, 2026
Anthropic’s August 2026 surveys found staff expect far faster AI progress than US adults: 91% expect Nobel-level discoveries by 2030, versus 39% of the public. Staff expect AI to handle 75% of their work hours by 2030, while US workers estimate 28%; model inputs imply median 2030 GDP growth of 17.1% for staff and 5.4% for US adults.
27.)
How Employment Is Changing at Anthropic
| Anthropic.com | October 16, 2026
Anthropic’s internal analysis says the share of junior technical hires fell from 27% to 9% since early 2025 as employee-directed AI agents reached six times human work hours by August 2026. It links adoption to higher output across engineering, sales, and legal, while arguing that attention, judgment, and managing agent pipelines have become the new constraints.
28.)
Mark Wahlberg on Using AI in Film ‘the Right Way’ and Being Open to an AI Clone Carrying on His Legacy
| TechCrunch.com | October 16, 2026
Mark Wahlberg said at TechCrunch Disrupt that he may use AI to enhance stadium scenes in an upcoming Pete Rose biopic, while rejecting AI-generated scripts and replacements for real actors. The actor and angel investor said he would consider an AI replica managed by his children or grandchildren, including one that could extend the Ted franchise.
October 15, 2026 📅️
29.)
Agentic Commerce: Why Your Wallet Is About To Change
| a16z | YouTube.com | October 15, 2026
Sitting down with Terry Angelos, Alex Rampell pulls apart the strategic angles behind AI agents that can make purchases on consumers’ behalf. Their conversation examines payment credentials, agentic tokens, merchant resistance, and the liability questions that arise when automated buying goes wrong.
30.)
AI Leaders Can’t Get Along. So How Will They Keep Us Safe? – With Kevin Roose
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | October 15, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI governance, Alex Kantrowitz speaks with Kevin Roose about whether an industry marked by rivalry and distrust can responsibly build systems that surpass human capabilities. Their conversation traces the power struggles at OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and Microsoft, alongside the risks posed by AI systems that may eventually improve themselves.
31.)
GPT-Live-1.1 Has New Voices And Better Accents
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | October 15, 2026
Showcasing GPT-Live-1.1, OpenAI outlines a voice update designed to improve accents and reduce unnecessary verbal checking. The release adds voices for French, German, Hindi, Mexican Spanish, Korean, and Japanese across ChatGPT, Codex, and dots, with API availability slated for later.
32.)
Build More Personal Sites With Codex
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | October 15, 2026
Showcasing new Codex capabilities, OpenAI demonstrates how teams can build sites that adapt to individual visitors while staying current. The workflow combines scheduled data refreshes with plugin connections, allowing site views to reflect both updated information and user-specific context.
33.)
ByteDance’s World Model Re-Shoots Movies, Sora Returns? & Krea 3 Is Here!
| Theoretically Media | YouTube.com | October 15, 2026
Cutting through the hype around ByteDance’s latest AI efforts, Theoretically Media examines an unreleased world model that can reframe a movie scene from newly drawn camera paths, alongside Krea 3 and reports of Sora’s possible return. The roundup also tracks OmniHuman 2.0, Pico Space Pro, World Gacha’s Blender-ready procedural towns, and LTX-2.5’s open-source post-production tools.
34.)
Anthropic Update on Independent Evaluators
| Anthropic.com | October 15, 2026
Anthropic has given six METR employees company hardware, office space, and roughly the same internal-tool access as its risk-assessment staff, in a voluntary third-party oversight pilot. METR can publish its assessments without Anthropic approval, though the company may require redactions in predefined categories; SecureBio, Accenture, and others are at earlier access tiers.
35.)
Bringing the Magic: Google Breaks Open a Bottleneck in Quantum Computing
| Blog.google | October 15, 2026
Google Quantum AI says it demonstrated magic state cultivation on its Willow processor, cutting errors roughly 40-fold versus uncultivated states and producing T-states with 99.99% logical fidelity. Published in Science, the result targets a resource bottleneck that can consume up to 95% of a fault-tolerant machine’s capacity.
36.)
Introducing Muse Spark Open, the Most Capable US Open-Weight Model to Date
| ResearchMeta.ai | October 15, 2026
Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816B-parameter (42B active) multimodal open-weight model with a 1M-token context window, aimed at coding and long-horizon agentic work. Meta says it can run on two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios via MLX, while weights are available through Hugging Face and other cloud catalogs.
37.)
Check if a Text Message Is a Scam Using Circle to Search
| Blog.google | October 15, 2026
Google says Circle to Search on Android can assess suspicious text messages before a link is opened or personal information is shared. Users can long-press the home button or navigation bar, circle a message, and receive an AI Overview with scam indicators, guidance, and suggested next steps; availability and compatibility may vary.
38.)
Frontier Pre-Training at Microsoft AI
| Microsoft.ai | October 15, 2026
Microsoft says it has completed pre-training MAI-Base-2, a mixture-of-experts foundation model with 80 billion active and 2.8 trillion total parameters. Trained on 16,000 GB200 GPUs for 38 days, the model reportedly beats every open-weight model Microsoft tested on held-out evaluations and is 4.2x to 12.3x more FLOPs-efficient than DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base.
39.)
Sylvester Stallone on AI in Hollywood: ‘It Makes Things So Much Easier’
| YahooFinance.com | October 15, 2026
Sylvester Stallone says AI de-aging could enable a Rambo prequel tracing the character from an 18-year-old recruit to a traumatized veteran. He points to de-aged performances in The Irishman and Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny, while acknowledging Hollywood’s concerns that AI could eliminate jobs.
40.)
AI Agents Are Coming to Rivian’s Cars
| TechCrunch.com | October 15, 2026
Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe said the automaker’s cars will eventually be able to run third-party AI agents from companies such as Anthropic, though he gave no timeline. Rivian’s in-house framework routes requests between local and cloud models while keeping agents away from safety-critical functions such as braking and steering.
41.)
Open From Data Center to Desktop: NVIDIA Expands Nemotron Family With Highest Efficiency Super VL and Bolt Models
| Blogs.NVIDIA.com | October 15, 2026
NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120-billion-parameter open vision-language model it says matches its largest reasoning model’s multimodal agentic accuracy at roughly one-fifth the parameters and delivers 5x the throughput of the next-best model in its class. It also launched Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB for local RTX/DGX Spark workloads; the 4GB Bolt E4B is due Oct. 23.
42.)
FLUX 3 Image Klein: Open Weights, 5.6B Parameters
| BFL.ai | October 15, 2026
Black Forest Labs released FLUX 3 Image Klein, a 5.6B-parameter open-weights image model supporting native 4K generation, pixel-perfect editing, bounding-box controls, and up to 10 reference images. Its INT8 build runs on NVIDIA RTX GPUs with 8GB of VRAM; API pricing starts at $0.009 per 1K image.
43.)
Introducing Instant Soundtracks
| ElevenLabs.io | October 15, 2026
ElevenLabs has launched Instant Soundtracks, which scores uploaded ElevenCreative videos with original music and timestamp-aligned sound effects. The release adds audio-as-reference controls and separate SFX layers; its Studio API supports add_sfx, separate_tracks, and use_audio_as_reference for up to 10 videos, 200 MB, and 10 minutes per request.
44.)
Amazon’s Bee Launches Two New Personal AI Devices, Starting at $75
| TechCrunch.com | October 15, 2026
Amazon-owned Bee has launched the $74.99 Frontier wearable and $99.99 Eclipse, a credit-card-sized recorder that attaches magnetically to a smartphone. The devices summarize conversations, produce to-dos and calendar items, and connect with Alexa, Amazon.com, Gmail, Google Calendar, and Microsoft Outlook; an $11.99 monthly Pro tier adds unlimited summaries and integrations.
October 14, 2026 📅️
45.)
I Tested AI Cloning… And It’s Way Worse Than You Think!
| Dave’s Garage | YouTube.com | October 14, 2026
Showcasing AI-assisted reverse engineering, Dave’s Garage walks viewers through the process of analyzing compiled software and rebuilding its behavior in a fresh application. The demonstration weighs what current models can infer from binaries against the engineering judgment still required, highlighting the technique’s practical limits and security implications.
46.)
Google Just Went Frontier (Gemini 4 Argon)
| Matthew Berman | YouTube.com | October 14, 2026
Cutting through the hype around Gemini 4 Argon, Matthew Berman examines what Google’s frontier model positioning reveals and why the release matters. He also considers its availability in Box and points to the model card as a key source for evaluating its capabilities and limits.
47.)
New Claude Motion Is Insane
| The AI Advantage | YouTube.com | October 14, 2026
Showcasing Claude Motion, The AI Advantage walks viewers through an end-to-end workflow for converting complex material into editable animations. The beta feature, available on Claude Team and Enterprise plans, includes controls for text, timing, images, color palettes, and brand styling.
48.)
Can Open Models Keep Up With OpenAI And Anthropic? | Nathan Lambert
| a16z | YouTube.com | October 14, 2026
Sitting down with Nathan Lambert, Lisha Li pulls apart whether open models can remain close to OpenAI and Anthropic as frontier training grows more expensive. Their exchange weighs compute limits, distillation, post-training, and the role of RL environments, while outlining how Trillium aims to make advanced AI research more observable.
49.)
How Hugging Face’s Investor Spots Winners
| Every | YouTube.com | October 14, 2026
Sitting down with Factorial Capital’s Matt Hartman, Natalia Quintero pulls apart the strategic angles behind Hugging Face’s evolution from a teen chatbot to a central hub for open-source AI. Hartman explains why technical founders can adapt when an initial concept fails, how portfolio companies feed Factorial’s deal flow, and why rapid iteration is reshaping the value of product insight.
50.)
Uber’s AI Infra, From The Inside
| The Pragmatic Engineer | YouTube.com | October 14, 2026
Cutting through the hype around agentic development, Gergely Orosz speaks with Uday Kiran Medisetty about the internal platforms Uber built to give AI agents access to code, services, and institutional knowledge. The conversation maps DevPods, Slate, MCP gateways, and context graphs onto everyday workflows, while examining token economics, code review, and productivity measurement as engineering roles shift.
51.)
Give Your Team AI Skills You Can Trust
| DeepLearningAI | YouTube.com | October 14, 2026
Showcasing its enterprise training program, DeepLearningAI outlines how organizations can build dependable AI capabilities across engineering teams. The program draws on analysis of more than 10,000 roles and expert interviews, positioning sustained learning as a response to a widening workplace skills gap.
52.)
What If Apps Didn’t Need Code?
| The Neuron | YouTube.com | October 14, 2026
Cutting through the hype around generated interfaces, Corey Noles and Grant Harvey examine Runway’s Solaris with co-founder Anastasis Germanidis. The conversation covers how interface world models could respond to inputs, maintain state, and extend beyond software into robotics, games, and personalized computing.
53.)
How $31 Trillion In Datacenters Get Built By 2050 – With Dallas Dolen
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | October 14, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI infrastructure, Alex Kantrowitz examines PwC’s projection of $31 trillion in global data-center investment through 2050 with Dallas Dolen. The conversation weighs whether rising compute demand can outpace efficiency improvements, where the electricity will come from, and how political resistance could reshape the global buildout.
54.)
Preparing for the 2026 US Midterms
| Anthropic.com | October 14, 2026
Anthropic is adding Democracy Works voting data and election-night results to Claude.ai while expanding classifiers for coordinated election abuse. Its analysis of 250,000 US conversations found 5.75% touched on politics, 0.51% concerned elections or voting, and just 0.002% violated election-integrity policies.
55.)
OpenAI Claims an Ex-Employee Took Its Product Plans and Presented Them to Apple
| TheVerge.com | October 14, 2026
OpenAI alleges a former employee copied more than 100 confidential files before joining Apple, then presented material including unreleased-device images, supplier data, engineering details, and hardware-finish reports to Apple leadership. The claim appears in the companies’ trade-secrets dispute; Apple did not immediately respond to The Verge.
56.)
